messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gpu-inference-pool-02 queue growing rapidly; autoscaler reports failures to expand (pool.max_gpus_reached).

maya: I'm on it. seeing queue ~18k reqs for pool-02, 99p latency ~4.2s, token throttles climbing.

kevin: are customers hitting errors? 5xx or 429?

maya: yes — 429 spikes and some 503s on /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. Support flagged timeouts from tenants.

incident-bot: autoscaler log excerpt: attempted scale at 1870109900 -> failure reason: \"pool.max_gpus_reached\". last successful scale at 1870101000.

oliver: metrics zoomed in: continuous_batching CPU wait up, and KV prefix cache miss rate jumped from ~2% to ~48% in the last hour.

chris: that smells like the batching/prefix-cache regression. did we ship any fleet-config changes recently?

maya: checking deploy history — there was a fleet-config push ~3h ago changing batching window and prefix cache limits.

kevin: paste the config diff.

maya: diff from config push: 

```\n- continuous_batching:\n-   enabled: true\n-   window_ms: 150\n+ continuous_batching:\n+   enabled: true\n+   window_ms: 1200\n\n- prefix_cache:\n-   max_keys: 500000\n+ prefix_cache:\n+   max_keys: 50000
```

oliver: dropping prefix_cache 10x explains the miss spike. increasing the batching window to 1200ms increases batch formation latency and KV cache churn — combined they tank throughput.

support-engine: affected tenants per alert: 12 tenants >5% error rate spike; 3 enterprise customers reported noticeable degradation. sending initial customer note.

maya: proposed mitigation steps: 1) revert prefix_cache.max_keys to 500000 immediately; 2) set continuous_batching.window_ms back to 150; 3) request +8 GPUs to pool-02 temporarily; 4) disable continuous batching for high-throughput routes (/v1/embeddings) while stabilizing.

kevin: agreed. I'll handle the GPU request and disabling batching for embeddings. Maya, can you do the config rollback?

maya: applying fleet-config rollback now. starting job fc-8721.

oliver: I'll patch runtime to reduce window_ms on pool-02 nodes.

infra-bot: gpu-request submitted (req-4433) for +8 GPUs to pool-02; provider ETA 5-8m.

chris: routing suggestion: temporarily shift latency-tier traffic to dedicated inference nodes and deprioritize background batch jobs to reduce pressure.

support-engine: sending customer message: "We're investigating throttling on inference endpoints; mitigation underway. ETA 10-15m."

customer-success: notified enterprise contacts and offered warm dedicated pool while we remediate.

incident-bot: fleet-config rollback job started (job_id: fc-8721). awaiting propagation.

maya: rollback applied — prefix_cache.max_keys = 500000. observability shows miss rate falling to ~18% and trending down.

kevin: GPUs provisioning. disabling batching on embeddings route now.

kevin: continuous batching disabled for /v1/embeddings -> immediate improvement in tail latency for embedding requests.

infra-bot: cloud GPUs provisioned and attached to pool-02 (+8) at 1870112000.

maya: queue length dropping 18k -> ~3.4k in 6 minutes. 429 errors down ~78%.

oliver: 99p latency back to ~1.1s for generate route. embeddings latencies normalized after disabling batching.

support-engine: quick impact summary for timeline: tenants affected: 12; enterprise customers: 3 reported production degradation; peak error rate ~9% on affected endpoints; mitigations: prefix_cache rollback, manual +8 GPUs, temporary batching disable.

chris: next steps / long-term fixes: - create internal ticket TICKET-4922 (owner: oliver) for root cause and test harness for fleet-config diffs; - add guardrail in fleet-config to prevent prefix_cache < 100k without approval; - autoscaler alert when max_gpus_reached prevents scale >2m; - introduce canary rollout for batching parameter changes.

maya: starting handoff. next on-call: oliver. handoff notes: rollback at ~1870111500; GPUs attached at 1870112000; embeddings batching disabled at 1870111600; queues draining, continue monitoring.

oliver: ack. I'll own the postmortem and follow up on TICKET-4922. will validate rollback on staging before reintroducing tuning.

support-engine: customers updated with follow-up; no active escalations.

incident-bot: INCIDENT mitigated. suspected root cause: fleet-config drift that lowered prefix cache and increased batching window, causing cache churn and throughput drop while autoscaler hit pool GPU cap. Postmortem assigned.

chris: add retro item to improve CI for fleet-config diffs. closing this thread; keep TICKET-4922 open until resolved.

maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
